Hi Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — Evergreen is seriously interested in the Redwood platform for our new lending product that will surface financial and educational records for a subset of our partners. Two quick asks to move vendor risk forward:

- Can you provide your proposed GLBA addendum and a high-level timeline to execute? Our procurement team needs to understand the path to contract (we typically run a 6–8 week external legal review).
- We also support a pilot with ScholarServe (education partner). Do you have FERPA-specific addenda or controls we can review?
- Please share your current subprocessor roster and a residency map (which subprocessors process data in the EU / US). Any planned subprocessors in the next 90 days would be helpful.
- Last: our security team wants to know if Redwood supports US-only data residency options and whether EU-US transfers require SCCs or other mechanisms.

Attachments: vendor-questionnaire-evg-20261001.pdf (we attached our vendor RFI)

If you can send a short prioritized plan (what we can get signed quickly vs. longer items), that would be ideal. Can we aim for a working draft of addenda and the subprocessor matrix by Oct 18?

Best,

Hi Samantha / Eliot — thanks for the clear asks. Looping in Monica (Legal), Marissa (Privacy) and Grace (Sales Ops) to scope an actionable plan. Quick response and proposed approach below.

Priority recommendation (practical sequencing):
1) GLBA addendum + full subprocessor matrix (high priority for Evergreen) — target working draft in 10 business days.
2) FERPA coverage for ScholarServe — run in parallel as a follow-on (different clause set; aim for a draft within 3 weeks).
3) BAA / HIPAA conversation only if you confirm PHI flows — we’ll slot that after GLBA if needed.

Immediate deliverables we will share:
- Draft GLBA addendum (with commercial redlines highlighted) — attachment: subprocessor_matrix_v1.xlsx and a short "priority rationale" doc.
- Subprocessor residency map (EU/US flags) and a proposed mitigation plan for any EU-hosted subprocessors.

Open questions for you (helps prioritize):
- Do you require US-only residency for Evergreen production data, or is pseudonymous EU processing acceptable with SCCs?
- For ScholarServe, is student data considered de-identifiable by your team or do you need FERPA-preserving controls (e.g., parental consent flows, data minimization)?

We’ll circulate a short redline and an internal gap analysis for legal to review. If Oct 18 for a consolidated package still works, we’ll aim for that. If you prefer a staged delivery (GLBA first via DocuSign, FERPA to follow), say the word and we’ll push GLBA to the top.

Attachments: subprocessor_matrix_v1.xlsx (draft), priority_rationale.md

—

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Regulated addenda + subprocessor disclosure request (GLBA / FERPA)

Jonas / team — reviewing Samantha's RFI and the draft matrix. High-level legal notes and risks:

- GLBA: we need explicit consumer financial data processing clauses, breach notification timelines (we usually push 72-hour notice to vendor), and permitted uses (analytics/aggregations must be contractually scoped). Evergreen will want indemnity caps tied to PCI/financial incidents — commercial will need to weigh that.
- FERPA: FERPA typically requires us to treat student records as educational records under contract with educational institutions. Clauses around parental rights, data subject requests, and de-identification need to be explicit. If ScholarServe processes minors, we should recommend terms around parental consent and data retention limits.
- Subprocessors: the matrix flags two EU-hosted inference accelerators (AccelX EU) used for quantized workloads. If Evergreen insists on US-only residency, we can propose routing their traffic to US-only clusters (Dedicated / Private) as an operational control.
- Transfers: we currently rely on SCCs for EU-US transfers; if a customer requires no cross-border transfers, our Private offering is the recommended mitigation.

Suggested next steps (legal):
1) Produce an initial GLBA redline (I attached legal_redlines_glba_ferpa.docx with comments inline).
2) Document required AWS region constraints and add a runbook for residency enforcement.
3) Prepare an optional BAA checklist (if any PHI risk surfaces).

Timing: we can have a legal-ready GLBA redline by Oct 15 if Sales agrees to the routing/residency approach. FERPA redline will take longer given student-data specifics — target Oct 29 for an initial legal draft.

Attachments: legal_redlines_glba_ferpa.docx (inline comments)

—
Monica Patel
Director, Legal & Privacy | Redwood Inference
